title: Solutions to False Results in Agglutination Tests for Infectious Diseases
author: Saxena, Chothe, et al.

steps.title: Collect serum samples
steps.instruction: Obtain blood from cattle or buffalo (age ≥ 2 years) at veterinary clinics, dairy farms or animal shelters around Ludhiana; separate serum or plasma and keep at 4 °C until testing. Select brucellosis‑suspected herds (history of abortions) and healthy herds (repeated RBPT‑negative status).

steps.title: Perform conventional RBPT (reference)
steps.instruction: On a clean glass slide, place 5 µl of RBPT coloured antigen (IVRI, Izatnagar, India) and 5 µl of the test serum; mix with a clean sterilised toothpick. After exactly 2 min observe the slide: clear clumps = positive, no clumps = negative.

steps.title: Stain test serum
steps.instruction: Add enough 0.1 % Coomassie Blue dye to the test serum (or plasma) to achieve a visible blue colour of the antibodies; mix gently until uniformly stained.

steps.title: Set up Superagglutination reaction
steps.instruction: On a clean glass slide, add the reagents in the following order and volume: 2.5 µl RBPT coloured antigen, 2.5 µl stained serum, 2.5 µl biotinylated anti‑bovine IgG (Sigma), 2.5 µl streptavidin (Sigma). Mix thoroughly on the slide.

steps.title: Incubate and observe
steps.instruction: Allow the slide to stand for 4 min. Observe the slide for clump formation; use an ordinary hand‑lens if needed. If the result is doubtful, view the slide under a low‑power (10×) inverted microscope to examine clump composition.

steps.title: Run assay controls
steps.instruction: Prepare two control reactions on separate slides: (a) Antibody control – antigen + negative serum + species‑specific antiglobulin (no agglutination expected); (b) Antiglobulin control – antigen + positive serum + unrelated antiglobulin (normal agglutination but no enhancement). Process these controls exactly as the test reaction.

steps.title: Interpret results
steps.instruction: Positive: clear agglutination containing both blue (antibody) and pink (antigen) colours visible on the slide or under the microscope. Negative: absence of such dual‑coloured agglutinates; presence of aggregates of only pink or only blue particles.
